If FDA grants a petition for a new cosmetic color, the listing regulation will be published in the Federal Register within 90 days after filing of the petition (or within 180 days if extended as provided in section 721(d)(1) of the act). The regulation will list the color additive in part 73 or 74 of this chapter on the appropriate list or lists, and it may specify the conditions under which the color additive may be safely used, including maximum quantities, specific food, drug, or cosmetic uses, methods of addition, and labeling requirements deemed necessary to assure safety. The regulation will only list the color additive for the use(s) for which it has been found suitable and safe; if not, the Commissioner shall by order deny the petition and notify the petitioner of such order and reasons. If the color additive is intended for use in meat, meat food product, or poultry product subject to FMIA or PPIA, the regulation must list any such uses where the color has been found suitable and safe. The regulation may exempt the color additive from batch certification if the Commissioner finds it unnecessary for public health protection, based on considerations of composition, manufacturing process, impurities, toxic potential, control procedures, and variability.

21 CFR 70.3(j) [7] defines "straight color" as a color additive listed in parts 73, 74, and 81 of this chapter, including lakes and substances permitted by the specifications for such color.

21 CFR 71.20(a) [2] requires that the regulation list the color additive in part 73 or 74 of this chapter on an appropriate list or lists as provided under section 721(b)(1).

21 CFR 71.20(a)(1) [3] specifies that the regulation may list the color additive for general use in or on foods, drugs, or cosmetics, or for coloring the human body, and may prescribe conditions such as maximum quantities of straight color or diluent, specific food, drug, or cosmetic classes, methods of addition, and labeling or packing requirements to assure safety.

21 CFR 71.20(a)(2) [4] requires that the regulation list the color additive only for uses for which it has been found suitable and safe; alternatively, the Commissioner may deny the petition with reasons.

21 CFR 71.20(a)(3) [5] mandates that if the color is to be used in meat, meat food product, or poultry product under FMIA or PPIA, the regulation must list such uses where the color has been found suitable and safe.

21 CFR 71.20(b) [6] provides that the Commissioner may exempt the color additive from batch certification if they find it unnecessary for public health protection, based on composition, manufacturing process, possible impurities, toxic potential, control and analytical procedures, and variability of composition.
